decisions.reason: False positive under the stated deterministic environment restriction: with trivial F_0, x_1 is fixed. Inductively, a complete history through t-1 is a deterministic function of (A_1,...,A_{t-1}), because each reward vector is a fixed deterministic function of the preceding complete history and X_s=x_{s,A_s}. Conversely the complete history records all those actions. Hence F_{t-1}=sigma(A_1,...,A_{t-1})=sigma(A_1,X_1,...,A_{t-1},X_{t-1}); requiring P_t to be F_{t-1}-measurable does not add hidden random feedback. The online-decision-protocol dependency separately requires a learner rule using only revealed history and private randomization; environment-specific measurability alone is not a claim that the learner knows the adversary rule. The estimates use only X_t and the known sampling probabilities. Finite histories and strictly positive probabilities give finite-valued integrable estimates. No extension to randomized reward environments is asserted.

Confirmed nonfatal citation attribution error: the generic filtration Definition supplies only nested sub-sigma-algebras, not the round-history interpretation asserted by F4. That interpretation is explicitly supplied by the already-declared estimator Definition, so the argument has no missing mathematical hypothesis. Repaired F4 to distinguish the generic structure from the estimator-specific history and added its exact estimator citation to the contract. On every positive-probability history atom H, y and p are constant and the estimator takes y/p with probability p and 0 otherwise. Thus its conditional first moment is y, second moment y^2/p, and centered second moment y^2(1-p)/p. The finite history tree and p>0 give bounded variables and squares; null atoms do not affect integral identities. The endpoints y=0, y=1 and p=1 are valid; p=0 is excluded. Statement, claim strength and dependencies are unchanged.
